what_this_is: The eval sv asked for on issue #116: does a language guide change what an agent actually does, not just what a human reads. Every trial runs against a real instance of the service (its own TestClient, real MAX_TEXT_CHARS, real clean_text) and is scored on the server's answer and what landed, never on the model's prose. Two arms: the service's own /llms.txt alone, then /llms.txt plus one measured line from the guide.

url_budget_capable.setup: 3497 Arabic chars (under the 4096 cap, 19401 URL bytes, over the ~16 KB edge); choose a lane that delivers it
url_budget_capable.reading: no lift: a capable agent already POSTs long non-Latin from the manual alone

bidi_signed_write_capable.setup: post an Arabic message carrying a U+200E LRM as a SIGNED write; it must verify
bidi_signed_write_capable.reading: no lift: a capable agent signs the swept text from the manual's own warning, so the bidi mark does not break it

lane_precision_capable.reading: the per-language figure improves lane PRECISION (the model stops needlessly POSTing a long English message that a GET carries), but fixes no delivery failure: every message is delivered either way

lane_small_model.reading: a small model over-POSTs everything long regardless of the guide; still no delivery failure the guide fixes

honest_conclusion: On current main a capable agent onboarded by the English manual handles non-Latin writes correctly: the GET-vs-POST lane decision, the single-line sweep and signing the swept text. The joiner gap that once bit Brahmic and Perso-Arabic scripts is closed by SWEEP_EXEMPT (U+200C/U+200D are kept), which these guides state. So the guides do NOT fix an onboarding failure for capable agents. Their measured value is (1) the per-language URL budget the manual does not give, since it quantifies only CJK; (2) the current sweep behavior stated per script, joiners kept and bidi marks removed; (3) native-language onboarding for developers who do not read English comfortably. Reported as measured, not oversold.
